node_definition.done_when:
The lead wants `reckon crew dispatch` fast. Measured on real ledger rows since 2026-10-03T06:10Z, across all mounted projects: 72 dispatches carried a picker_selection. Of these, 56 routed, 1 held and 15 (21%) timed out at the 5 s PICKER_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS bound and fell back to the default lane. Median pick latency_ms was 4142 and p90 5005. The Jev call itself (jev_latency_ms) is 0.3–0.5 s every time.

Latency is bimodal by project. Nova picks take about 1.6–2.0 s. Reckon picks take 4.2–4.8 s or time out, with an occasional 0.9 s. Several caching nodes already landed: a context window measured once, stamp-keyed cross-process caches for run-time profiles (reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py), and pure-file pick inputs (reckon/capabilities.py cached_pick_input, routing._verdict_input_stamp, agent_context). All are keyed on ledger and file stamps. A likely cause, which you must confirm or refute by measurement, is that reckon's ledger takes a promotion every few minutes. Each promotion moves the stamp, so every cache misses and the next pick re-reads the whole ledger (about 1,567 per-run files and 76 MB on GPFS). Separately, before the bound starts, dispatch.py spends about 3.8 s in _picker_ledger_rows (ledger.runs) and about 3.9 s in _picker_budget_snapshot (budget.preflight) on a cold dispatch.

Goal: a cold `reckon crew dispatch` for project reckon reaches the worker launch quickly, and its pick never times out.
1. Measure first, in a fresh process for each sample, with phase timings for the whole CLI dispatch path up to the launch: flight resolution, picker input build, pick, availability probe, plan_dispatch, preflight and worktree creation. Use `--dry-run` for repeatable samples, plus at least three real dispatch-path pick measurements. Cover project reckon and project nova, and repeat while the reckon ledger is gaining new run files, which you can simulate by adding fixture run files to a copy. Record the phase table from tool output in docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/dispatch-speed.html, with a figure.
2. Remove the dominant costs. Make ledger-derived inputs incremental rather than all-or-nothing: an index that reads only run files newer than its last read, persisted across processes under the existing RECKON_HOME-first cache root, written atomically, with a corrupt index treated as a miss. Do the same for anything that recomputes over the whole ledger on the dispatch path (run_time_profile, the budget snapshot's recorded readings, the shared verdict inputs' ledger freshness key). Never cache a live reading such as availability, lane load, or budget pace against the current time.
3. Targets, measured on this workstation for project reckon: the pick step p90 at or below 1.5 s over 20 or more samples, including samples taken after a new run file lands, with zero timeouts; and the picker input build before the bound at or below 1.0 s when the ledger has gained only a few runs since the last read. If a target cannot be met, report the measured floor and the phase that holds it.
4. Equivalence: every input the picker receives, and the selection inputs that are rendered, must equal an uncached full build on the same fixture, including after appending and after editing a run file. Prove it with tests.
5. Fold in two review follow-ons of picker-fresh-process-pick. Add a test that edits a run file in place and asserts the shared verdict inputs recompute. Correct the agent_context.py comment that claims the stamp and the computation cannot drift.

Tests: tests/test_dispatch_speed.py and any focused file you need. Gate: those files, tests/test_picker*.py, tests/test_run_time_profile.py, tests/test_ledger*.py and tests/test_budget*.py, run with the main checkout's .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 in the FOREGROUND, with one log for base and one for head under the run directory, each ending in an EXIT line, judged by delta. The coordinator runs the full dispatch population at merge. Do not background anything. If you run out of time, commit what is measured and working and write the manifest with the remaining phases named.
